Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the SolaraTech Renewables Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants are reminded to mute your lines when not speaking to minimize background noise. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss SolaraTech Renewables's results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Financial Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Nina Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Liam Chen, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 2024 performance, driven by our continued focus on innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability. We are seeing strong demand for our renewable energy solutions across all markets.

Here are six key highlights from the quarter. First, our construction pipeline advanced significantly, with over 5.2 GW in backlog and 3.1 GW in advanced development, energizing 1.4 GW year-to-date—a 25% increase—supported by IRA incentives, and key projects like Desert Bloom Solar on track for December COD. Second, debt levels were well-managed at $7.8 billion gross, net debt at 3.4x EBITDA, with financing costs down to 4.2% through refinancings and green bonds. Third, we raised capacity addition guidance to 5.8 GW for FY2024 and 7.5 GW for FY2025, backed by a 52 GW pipeline across shovel-ready, advanced, and early-stage projects. Fourth, revenue surged 48% year-over-year to $1.28 billion, with EBITDA up 62% and margins at 30.1%, driven by segments like solar EPC and storage. Fifth, capacity factors improved fleet-wide, with solar at 28.2%, wind at 41.3%, and storage utilization at 28.4%, outperforming benchmarks through tech upgrades. Sixth, capital recycling delivered $850 million from asset sales, recycling into high-return pipeline projects.

Now, I will turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. We are very pleased with our financial performance in the Q3 2024. Revenue was $1.42 billion, a 48% increase year-over-year. This increase was driven by higher project commissioning and energy sales. Gross margin was 29.5%, reflecting improved cost management and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $285 million, primarily due to increased investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $225 million, or $0.98 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.75 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Let me expand on those highlights Elena mentioned, starting with our construction progress and commercial operation dates, which form a cornerstone of our growth strategy. We maintain a robust backlog exceeding 5.2 GW across utility-scale solar PV, hybrid solar-plus-storage, and onshore wind projects, plus 3.1 GW in advanced-stage development. Year-to-date, we've brought online 1.4 GW, up 25% from last year, thanks to smooth supply chains and benefits from the Inflation Reduction Act's Section 45X PTC and ITC transferability.

Key projects include our flagship 450 MW Desert Bloom Solar in Riverside County, California—our biggest CAISO-connected asset—at 92% mechanical completion. The 200 MWh BESS using Tesla Megapack 2XL is grid-synchronized ahead of schedule, with full COD set for December 15, 2024, using LONGi 650 Wp bifacial TOPCon modules and Nextracker trackers. It has a 20-year PPA with Southern California Edison at $28/MWh blended, protecting against CAISO's $45/MWh YTD spot volatility from heatwaves.

In Texas, the 800 MW Lone Star Hybrid in ERCOT West Hub—600 MWdc solar, 200 MW/800 MWh storage—is 78% complete on civil works. We addressed avian study delays with AI bird diverters and U.S. Fish and Wildlife collaboration. The 200 MW Vestas V150-4.2 MW wind portion is 60% erected, first power in Q1 2025, full COD June 30, 2025, under a Google corporate PPA at $32/MWh all-in, plus $15 million annual ancillary upside from frequency regulation.

Midwest's 300 MW Prairie Winds in Oklahoma is at 85% completion, accelerated 15% via Mortenson partnership with modular towers like NextEra's. Siemens Gamesa SG 5.0-145 DD blades are ramping; COD April 1, 2025, hedged with AEP Oklahoma at $25/MWh, capturing full PTC $27/MWh plus 10% domestic bonus.

Internationally, Europe's 250 MW Solara Iberica in Spain's Extremadura is 65% done, EPC to Acciona EnergÃ­a nearly finished, with 2,300 kWh/kWp yields using Enphase IQ8 microinverters. COD shifts to Q3 2025 for CBAM tweaks, but 15-year CfD with Endesa at â‚¬22/MWh. In APAC, 400 MW Australian pipeline including SunRay in Queensland is 45% through geotech, COD H2 2026 under LGC and VRET.

Portfolio-wide, construction capex is $2.8 billion of $4.1 billion budget, 95% on track with steel at $650/ton and polysilicon at $9/kg. Our Fast-Track 90 initiative standardizes 90-day grid timelines with Array pre-fab racking and IRA-qualified sourcing. 98% panels locked through 2025, diversified 55% U.S., 25% Europe, 20% APAC/Oceania. Hybrids now 40% of pipeline at 12%+ IRRs. We anticipate 2.5 GW CODs in FY25 for 35% EBITDA growth, deleveraging to 3.2x.

Turning to debt levels and financing costs, our investment-grade BBB+/Baa1 balance sheet supports our 20 GW pipeline. Total gross debt at quarter-end was $7.8 billion: $4.2 billion project finance, $2.1 billion corporate revolver/term, $1.5 billion green bonds. Down from $8.1 billion year-start after $450 million amortizations and $150 million prepays. Net debt $6.6 billion, 3.4x trailing EBITDA of $1.95 billion, target 3.0-4.0x, below peers.

Interest expense guided $320-340 million, 4.2% blended cost, down 110 bps from 2022 via refinancings. Q3 highlights: $1.2 billion green loan for DesertBloom at SOFR +140 bps, tightened 75 bps with IRA tax equity at 7.5% yields; â‚¬500 million 12-year green bond at 3.75%, 25 bps tight, SBTi-linked. U.S. (65% EBITDA) at 3.9%, Europe 4.6%, APAC 3.2%. Hedging 70% variable to fixed at 3.8%; $1.1 billion ITC monetized; $15 billion forward fund at 4.0%. Tailwinds for $1 billion refinance at <4%.

Now, on revenue and earnings growth: Q3 revenue $1.28 billion, +48% YoY, +12% QoQ, ninth accelerating quarter from $18.5 billion backlog +35% YoY, IRA $185 million boost. EBITDA $385 million +62% YoY, 30.1% margins +420 bps; EPS $0.92 +65%; net income $210 million; FCF $290 million for buybacks/dividends.

Segments: Solar EPC $665 million +55%, 2.8 GWdc including Desert Sun COD at $28/MWh LCOE, 45% ITC; Storage $358 million +72%, 1.5 GWh for Microsoft; Wind $192 million +25%, 850 MW hybrids; O&M $65 million +30%, 15 GW managed.

Regions: North America 68% $870 million +52%, IRA $120 million; EMEA 22% +38%; APAC 10% +65%. Gross margins 28.5% +510 bps; FY24 guide $5.3-5.5 billion revenue, $1.45-1.55 billion EBITDA.

Capacity factors: Solar 28.2% +150 bps YoY (12.5 GW), trackers/bifacial; U.S. Southwest 31.4%, Texas 26.8%, Australia 29.1%. Wind 41.3% (20.5 GW), onshore 38.7%, offshore 53.2%. Storage 28.4% utilization, 92.3% RTE (8 GWh). Blended 35.6%, 22.5 TWh generation.

Capital recycling: $850 million Q3 from 450 MW sales. Desert Bloom 250 MW to BlackRock at $1.45/W, 14.2% IRR; Windridge 200 MW to Brookfield/SWF at $1.8 million/MW. YTD 25% of $2.5 billion goal, recycled to 3.2 GW pipeline. Guide $3-3.5 billion 2025.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Jordan for our project pipeline update.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Marcus. Our project pipeline continues to grow, with 52 GW under development. We are making good progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, guiding 5.8 GW FY24 additions (3.9 GW solar, 1.2 GW wind, 0.7 GW BESS), 7.5 GW FY25, up to 11 GW FY27 for 33 GW cumulative CAGR 32%. Shovel-ready 14.2 GW, advanced 22.8 GW (top PJM/MISO queues, UK offshore), early 15 GW (India/Australia). 65% U.S., 20% Europe, 15% APAC. Solar 55%, wind 25%, BESS 20%. We are also actively exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

Next, Dr. Patel will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Dr. Nina Patel:
Thank you, Jordan. We are committed to developing and deploying innovative technologies that improve the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy systems. We are making significant progress on our research and development efforts, including advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. We believe that these technologies will play a critical role in accelerating the transition to a clean energy future. The development of our perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells is expected to boost module efficiencies beyond 30%, reducing LCOE by over 20% and enabling higher yields in hybrid configurations across our pipeline.

And now, Liam will provide an update on our sustainability efforts.

Liam Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are committed to operating our business in a sustainable manner and minimizing our environmental impact. We have set ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that promote sustainability. We believe that sustainability is not only the right thing to do but also makes good business sense.

I'll now turn the call back to Elena for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Liam. In closing, we are confident that SolaraTech Renewables is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for Q&A. Our first question comes from Sarah Kim with GreenInvest. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
Can you provide more details on the regulatory environment for renewable energy projects in your key markets?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Sarah. The regulatory landscape remains supportive overall. In the U.S., the IRA continues to drive momentum with PTC/ITC transferability and domestic content adders, helping us accelerate 65% of our pipeline despite interconnection queues—we've climbed top positions in PJM/MISO through restudies. Europe's REPowerEU and net-zero mandates aid our 20% exposure, though CBAM and permitting tweaks caused minor COD slips in Spain. APAC benefits from India's 500 GW target and Australia's VRET, with stable frameworks. Risks like avian studies or grid upgrades are managed via partnerships and lobbying; overall, policy tailwinds outweigh headwinds for our diversified portfolio.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with EcoCapital. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly:
How is the company addressing the challenges of energy storage integration with your renewable energy projects?

Dr. Nina Patel:
Great question, Tom. Integration challenges like dispatch optimization and degradation are core to our R&D. We've co-located BESS on 40% of solar sites, using LFP and flow batteries for 4-8 hour durations, achieving 92% RTE and 28% utilization via AI platforms like our Aurora system for frequency regulation and arbitrage. Hybrids boost system CF 5-7 points, monetizing ERCOT/CAISO ancillaries at $15-20/MWh. We've deployed active balancing to limit aging to 1.2% annually, partnering with Tesla and CATL, and our Nevada gigafactory scales to gigawatt-hours with IRA incentives. This de-risks intermittency, lifts IRRs to 12%+, and positions us for hyperscaler demand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with RenewBank. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What are your expectations for the long-term growth of the renewable energy market?

Elena Vasquez:
Lisa, we're bullish on 25-30% sector CAGR through 2030, per IEA Net Zero pathways, driven by $370B IRA, EU Green Deal, and corporate PPAs from tech giants covering 5-10 GW annually. Tightening grids, data center loads, and decarbonization mandates fuel demand; our 52 GW pipeline targets 45 GW operational by 2030, capturing 15% U.S. utility share via scale, tech like tandems, and recycling for 15% FFO/share CAGR. Policy evolution like Article 6 greens and supply chain resilience will sustain this, with our diversified tech/regional mix buffering volatility.

Operator:
Instructions. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in SolaraTech Renewables. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
